lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write one clarifying and one evidence-based response line for a talk on longer recess.

FEEDBACK
Clarify a detail; respond with a fact or reasoned link.

CHECK
Only nodding without content is not a full response.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Listen to a short talk, ask two clarifying questions and give one evidenced response. Record your notes.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Listen to a short talk, ask two clarifying questions and give one evidenced response. Record your notes. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using listen on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Only nodding without content is not a full response.. Correction: Clarify a detail; respond with a fact or reasoned link.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Only nodding without content is not a full response. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating listen on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with listen, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about listen with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for listen. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

WORKED MODEL

teach_steps.explain:
Listening and responding means noting a speaker’s claim, asking a clarifying question and answering with evidence rather than only agreeing.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
